runtime.backend: CSS perspective adaptation of source WebGL geometry

passes: DOM image planes projected with CSS perspective

timeline.deltaRule: dt capped after interruptions; exponential damping derived from source 0.92 at 60Hz
timeline.random: None in baseline; existing app random avatar assignment remains.

inputs.pointer: hover slows rotation; drag added in adaptation
inputs.scroll: Source deltaY * .004 spin, .002 vertical translation; adaptation lets normal page scroll pass through.
inputs.resize: Projection recomputed from container height; design scales intentionally differ.

output.domComposite: transparent local avatar PNGs; final warm paper and pastel cards requested by user

evidence.notes: Home renders FiberScene; one Canvas owns ImageTube, GridPlane and HelmetModel. ImageTube JSX and useFrame bind cylindrical planes, camera, wheel and damping.
Single fullscreen canvas; three visible rings of images, scrolling translates and rotates the rings. No iframe or video. Browser only supports read-only evaluation, so ablation/preload unavailable.

leafFacts.fact: radius 4; tile .72 x 1; row spacing 2.7; 5 x 12; camera z6.5 and fov50
Final card proportions, colors, number of rings and interaction sensitivity
leafFacts.notes: Intentional product design adaptation, not claimed as exact extraction.

wiringFacts.fact: row rotation = angle * (0.65 + row/(rows-1)*0.9); alternate half-column offset; inertia damping pow(.92, dt*60)
CSS projected DOM planes replace WebGL meshBasicMaterial; readable reverse sides and finite unique friends
wiringFacts.notes: Explicitly approximate adaptation to keep actual accessible controls and zero external dependencies.

important: CSS backface/compositing differs from WebGL. No helmet, technical grid, audio, or repeated infinite vertical rows in final design.

replay.fidelityTier: Source-informed cylindrical gallery adaptation, not a pixel-identical shader extraction
fallbacks: Use local avatar assets instead of external photography; CSS 3D instead of React/Three. These are intentional scope choices.
